text:
alex: hey team — weird one, my phone just died mid-flight. I left it in airplane mode for takeoff and it's not reconnecting. I might miss pages for the 02:00-05:00 UTC window. can someone pick up primary? :grimacing:

priya: I can take primary from ~02:10 until 05:00 UTC. grabbing the pager now. alex, do you have any running maintenance windows?

alex: no scheduled maints. only thing: there's a low-traffic canary running on embeds (stable-q2) for apac, but nothing user-impacting afaik. if something pages, it's likely latency spike or node OOMs.

oncall-bot: INCIDENTBOT: Pager triggered for team redwood-inference-primary at 2025-11-21T02:05:12Z — route: primary — severity: P3 — source: autoscaler — alert: high p95 latency on embed-frontend (2.3s).

priya: got the incidentbot ping. taking it. first step: triage latency, check autoscaler and node memory. david, lia — can one of you confirm the current autoscaler config in prod?

david: i pulled the autoscaler group. config looks normal: min=3, max=20, scaleWindow=60s. recent spikes show one node hitting OOMs and getting recycled ~02:03. suspect noisy batch job.

lia: i'm seeing repeat `OOMKilled` on inference-worker-3 in cluster inference-prod-1. logs show a batch job that requested 48GB but node is 40GB. suspect misconfigured batch from analytics.

priya: good catch. mitigation plan: 1) cordon and replace the bad node, 2) apply a quick autoscaler bump to keep p95 under target, 3) set a temporary reject policy for heavy analytics batch jobs. i'm running commands now.

priya: running runbook snippet — monitoring: ```kubectl get pods -n inference | egrep "OOMKilled|CrashLoopBackOff"```
priya: results: `inference-worker-3 OOMKilled`, `inference-batcher-7 Running`

priya: cordoning node `gke-infer-3` and draining safe pods (will respect PDB): ```kubectl cordon gke-infer-3 && kubectl drain gke-infer-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

ops-bot: OPSBOT: Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/oncall-primary-swap — checklist for node drain, autoscaler bump, and fallback routing.

david: i'm notifying analytics infra to hold heavy batches for 30m. pinged @analytics-team with request id `AN-4521`.

lia: after drain, replicas recovered and latency dropped to 780ms within 2 minutes. embedding error rate stable.

priya: confirming — p95 now 0.78s. setting a temporary route fallback: smaller-embed-v1 for new requests to avoid warmup penalty. command: `rl route set embed-frontend --fallback smaller-embed-v1 --weight 0.15`

alex: (late but reading) thanks all — priya appreciate the takeover. i updated my status to OOO in calendar and OpsPager with note "flight, unavail until 05:00 UTC".

priya: quick housekeeping before handoff: i updated the rotation in OpsPager to show me as primary from 02:10-05:00, and added runbook pointer in the thread. please ACK if you saw the schedule change.

david: ACK. noted analytics hold. i'll keep watch for retries causing a second wave.

lia: ACK, will check logs for retry storms and patch any misconfigured job definitions.

priya: leaving a short checklist for whoever takes over after 05:00: - verify node pool health `gcloud compute instances list` - check p95/p99 in Grafana dashboard `inference->embeds->latency` - confirm no queued analytics batches >10GB - rollback fallback routing if p95 stable <1s for 15 minutes

priya: handing off primary to alex at 05:00 UTC in OpsPager. hitting :white_check_mark: on the thread, will post final status at 04:55 UTC.

oncall-bot: INCIDENTBOT: Incident resolved for alert high p95 latency on embed-frontend at 2025-11-21T02:18:09Z — status: mitigated — notes: drained node, autoscaler stabilized, temporary fallback route applied.

alex: thanks team. i'll take back at 05:00 and confirm in ops-pager. if anyone sees residual retries after 03:30 please ping me on slack DM since my phone might still be flaky.

priya: final note — no customer-facing SLO breach expected (estimated impact <0.5% user requests and only transient). filed a follow-up ticket `OPS-1259` to block analytics batch that requested too much memory.

lia: added logs link: https://logs.redwood/trace/2871 — contains OOM stack and offending job id.

david: closing loop, will monitor until 05:10 then remove my watch. thanks all. :thumbsup:
